parsed.n_justification: To systematically evaluate runoff/recharge partitioning across clay content from 5% to 55%, we use 11 columns at 5% increments (5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%, 35%, 40%, 45%, 50%, 55%). This provides sufficient resolution to capture nonlinear hydraulic responses across the texture spectrum from sandy (5%) to clay-dominated (55%) soils. All columns share identical climate forcing, vegetation, and topography to isolate the clay content effect. A single representative mid-latitude location is used with forcing replicated across all columns.

elm_config.description: Controlled clay content sensitivity experiment with daily hydrology outputs

requires_capabilities: ELM single-column mode with custom soil texture specification
Ability to override default soil properties (clay/sand/silt percentages) for each column
Standard ELM hydrology with Richards equation or similar infiltration scheme
Output of surface runoff (saturation excess + infiltration excess) and subsurface drainage
Daily output frequency for water balance closure verification
assumptions: All columns use identical atmospheric forcing from the same location (40°N, 105°W - Colorado Front Range representative climate)
Vegetation type, LAI, and rooting depth held constant across all columns
Topography (slope) set to zero or minimal value to isolate texture effects
Soil depth and layer structure identical across columns
Soil organic matter content held constant
No lateral flow between columns (independent single-column simulations)
Hydraulic parameters (saturated hydraulic conductivity, water retention curves) derived from clay/sand/silt fractions using standard pedotransfer functions (e.g., Clapp-Hornberger or van Genuchten)
Initial soil moisture conditions identical across columns (cold start from default)
No human water management (irrigation, drainage tiles)
Recharge defined as QDRAI (subsurface drainage reaching water table or model bottom)
Runoff defined as QOVER (surface runoff from saturation and infiltration excess)
19-year simulation provides adequate sample of interannual climate variability
First 1-2 years may show spinup effects but are retained for water balance analysis
